outcome: Need for antihypertensive medication in the postpartum period
cohort: 200 preeclamptic women (100 requiring postpartum antihypertensive medication and 100 not requiring medication)
finding: In women with preeclampsia, the development of eclampsia, use of prophylactic magnesium sulfate, and high peak antenatal systolic blood pressure were significantly associated with an increased need for antihypertensive medication in the postpartum period.
mod_finding: While the abstract doesn't directly investigate mode of delivery, it notes a higher cesarean section rate in women requiring postpartum antihypertensives, suggesting a potential indirect link.
gest_age: Comparable gestational age at delivery between groups (34.3 vs. 35.6 weeks, p=0.220)
